{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "High frequency of vital signs assessments",
      "quote": "Vital Signs |  | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Vital signs are collected at every visit, including all 15 post-screening visits, which may be excessive and burdensome for patients, especially for a chronic condition study.",
      "fix": "Consider reducing vital signs to key visits (e.g., baseline, each dosing visit, and EOS) or allow remote monitoring for stable patients."
    },
    {
      "title": "Physical exam and ECG only at sparse visits",
      "quote": "Physical Exam |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |  |  |  |  | X | X | X",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Physical exam and ECG are only performed at screening, week 16, and EOS, which may miss safety signals that could appear between these long intervals, especially for a biologic with potential cardiac effects.",
      "fix": "Add physical exam and ECG at more frequent intervals, such as every 4 weeks, or at least at each dosing visit."
    },
    {
      "title": "Ophthalmological exam only at screening and EOS",
      "quote": "Ophthalmological Exam |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Ophthalmological exam is only at screening and EOS, but if the drug has potential ocular toxicity, more frequent monitoring may be needed. Also, the exam is not performed at baseline (Day 1) which could miss baseline abnormalities.",
      "fix": "Add ophthalmological exam at baseline and at periodic intervals (e.g., every 12 weeks) if there is any known ocular risk."
    },
    {
      "title": "PK sampling at every visit after baseline",
      "quote": "Serum REGN3500 Concentration (PK) |  |  | X | X | X |  | X |  | X |  | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "PK samples are collected at nearly every visit (14 out of 15 post-baseline visits), which is excessive for a monoclonal antibody with a long half-life and adds patient burden and cost.",
      "fix": "Reduce PK sampling to sparse visits (e.g., trough at each dosing visit and a few post-dose timepoints) to minimize burden."
    },
    {
      "title": "ADA sampling only at sparse visits",
      "quote": "Anti-REGN3500 Antibody (ADA) |  |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X |  |  |  |  | X | X | X",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "ADA is only collected at weeks 2, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, and 36, but not at EOT (week 16) or EOS (week 36) consistently? Actually it is at EOT and EOS, but missing at many intermediate visits where PK is collected, making it hard to correlate ADA with PK changes.",
      "fix": "Align ADA sampling with PK sampling at key visits (e.g., at least at each PK visit) to assess immunogenicity impact."
    },
    {
      "title": "Biomarker sampling frequency may be excessive",
      "quote": "hs-CRP, SAA |  | X | X |  | X |  | X |  | X |  | X |  |  |  | X | X | X | X",
      "page": 46,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Biomarkers like hs-CRP and SAA are collected at many visits (10 post-baseline), which may be unnecessary for a chronic disease and adds patient burden and cost.",
      "fix": "Reduce biomarker sampling to key efficacy timepoints (e.g., baseline, week 16, and EOS) or align with primary endpoint assessments."
    },
    {
      "title": "Tight postdose vital sign window",
      "quote": "Vital signs (sitting blood pressure, pulse, and respiration rate) should be taken predose and 30 minutes (±10 minutes) postdose (see Table 2).",
      "page": 53,
      "section": "8.2.3.1 Vital Signs",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The 30-minute postdose vital sign with a ±10-minute window is very tight and may be difficult to achieve in a busy clinic, leading to protocol deviations and potential data quality issues.",
      "fix": "Widen the postdose window to ±30 minutes or allow flexibility for real-world clinic flow."
    },
    {
      "title": "ECG before blood draw may cause delays",
      "quote": "Electrocardiograms (ECGs) should be performed before blood is drawn during visits requiring blood draws.",
      "page": 54,
      "section": "8.2.3.4 Electrocardiogram",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Requiring ECG before blood draw at every visit with both procedures may increase visit duration and patient burden, especially if ECG is only at sparse visits but blood draws are frequent.",
      "fix": "Clarify that ECG is only required at visits where both are scheduled, and allow flexibility in order if clinically appropriate."
    }
  ]
}
